2. Heard Sri Navin Kumar, holding brief of Sri Rajesh Kumar, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Joveen Kumar Singh, learned counsel for the informant as well as Sri Anit Kumar Shukla,
learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.
3. Applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No. 25 of 2024, under Sections 498A, 304B IPC and Section 3/4 of D.P. Act, Police Station Bhadohi, District Bhadohi, during the pendency of trial.
4. As per prosecution story, marriage of the applicant was solemnized with the deceased person as per Hindu rites on 21.05.2022.
The applicant and other family members are stated to have subjected the deceased to cruelty for demand of motorcycle as dowry and thereby led her to death on 22.02.2024 at about 11 a.m.
5. Learned counsel for the applicant has argued that the applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.
He has nothing to do with the said offence as alleged in the FIR.
The FIR is delayed and there is no explanation of the said delay caused.

6. Learned counsel has further stated that the Investigating Officer had taken into consideration the CDR of the applicant which are on record and the applicant was in Mumbai at the time of offence and had returned back to his paternal home later on.
7.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 17.10.2024.
The trial is moving at snail's pace as only one witness has been examined to date and there is no likelihood of early conclusion of trial in near future.
The applicant has no criminal history.

In case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail and shall cooperate with trial.
8.
Per contra, learned AGA as well as learned counsel for the informant have vehemently opposed the bail application.

sentences.text: This Court had called for a report regarding the status of trial and in compliance thereof, a report has been submitted by the Trial Court concerned dated 06.08.2025.
As per the said report, one witness has been examined to date and the trial is moving on.

The delay in trial is due to death of one of the accused Sumitra Devi @ Sunita, as such trial stands abated against the said accused Sumitra Devi @ Sunita after recording the statement of court witness no.1 S.I. Brijesh Kumar Rai.

10. The Supreme Court in case of X Vs. State of Rajasthan & Anr. reported in 2024 INSC 909, has held that once the trial has commenced, it should be allowed to reach to its final conclusion, which may either result in conviction or acquittal of the accused.

entities.text: X Vs. State of Rajasthan & Anr. reported in 2024 INSC 909
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The bail should not be normally granted to the accused after the charge has been framed.
It should also not be granted by looking into the discrepancies here or there in the deposition.

11. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions advanced by learned counsel for the parties and also considering the status of trial and the period of incarceration undergone by the applicant being less than one year, I do not find it a fit case to release the applicant on bail.
12. The bail application is, accordingly, rejected.

13. However, it is directed that the aforesaid case pending before the trial court be decided expeditiously, in view of the principle laid down in the recent judgements of the Supreme Court in the cases of Vinod Kumar vs. State of Punjab 2015 (3) SCC 220 and Hussain and Another vs. Union of India (2017) 5 SCC 702, if there is no legal impediment.
